checklist.step: Scope which entities owe a certification and to whom
actions: Pull the insurer legal-entity register from the Corporate Secretary with each entity's state of domicile and NAIC co-code.

For each domiciliary state, read the enacted Section 4(i) analogue in the variance appendix and record whether certification is required, the due date (February 15 in the model; some states vary), the required filer (insurer vs all licensees) and the delivery channel.
Record any state whose adoption omits the certification requirement so the file shows the negative conclusion was reached deliberately.
Load one tracker row per required entity/state pair with the due date.
checklist.done: every legal entity has a tracker row stating certification required or not, with due date, channel and citation.

checklist.step: Open the certification cycle by November 15
actions: Kick off the cycle workplan at T-92 with the milestone chain: evidence complete January 15, counsel draft January 25, execution February 1, submission February 10, buffer to February 15.
Assign evidence-assembly owners: Security GRC Analyst (program artifacts), IT Security Manager (control metrics), Incident Response Lead (event register).
Verify the tracker reminders (T-90/T-60/T-30/T-14/T-7/T-3) are armed against each state's due date.
Brief the CISO on the calendar and any state whose requirement changed since last cycle.
checklist.done: the cycle is open by November 15 with owned milestones and armed reminders for every entity/state pair.

checklist.step: Assemble the support file from the year's program evidence
actions: Compile into the certification support file: the approved WISP and board report (REG-052-C01), the completed risk assessment and remediation ledger (REG-052-C02), the monthly control metrics and exception register (REG-052-C03) and the cybersecurity-event register with notification proofs (REG-052-C04).
Index each document against the statement clause it supports so the certification is traceable line by line.
Flag any missing or stale artifact to the Compliance Manager by January 15 — an evidence hole found in February is a crisis.
File the indexed support file under REG-052-C05/<year>.
checklist.done: an indexed support file maps every certification clause to current-year evidence, complete by January 15.

checklist.step: Collect control-owner attestations
actions: Issue attestation requests through the GRC platform to each Section 4(d) control owner asking them to confirm their control operated as designed through the certification year or to disclose exceptions.
Set a 10-business-day response window with escalation to the IT Security Manager for non-responders.
Reconcile disclosed exceptions against the GRC exception register — an owner disclosing a problem the register missed is itself a finding.
Attach the completed attestations to the support file.
checklist.done: every control owner has attested or disclosed, reconciled against the exception register, inside the window.

checklist.step: Document areas requiring improvement with remediation efforts
actions: Review the open exceptions, risk acceptances and audit findings across REG-052-C01 to C04 and identify any area, system or process requiring material improvement, redesign or update.

For each, document the remediation efforts planned and underway per Section 4(i)'s requirement to keep such records available for the commissioner — certifying is permitted while gaps exist only when the remediation record stands behind it.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether any gap is severe enough to qualify the certification language for a given state.
File the deficiency-and-remediation memorandum in the support file.
checklist.done: a deficiency memorandum documents every material gap with its remediation record and a counsel-agreed effect on the statement.

checklist.step: Draft each state's certification to its required form
actions: Draft the written statement per state certifying compliance with the state's information-security-program requirements, using the state's prescribed form or format where one exists and the model-act language otherwise.
Verify the named certifying entity, NAIC co-code, certification period and signing officer title match the state's enacted requirement.
Incorporate any qualification agreed in the deficiency review rather than certifying flat over a known material gap.
Route the drafts to the CISO with the support-file index for line-by-line factual confirmation.
checklist.done: per-state drafts on the correct forms carry accurate entity data and agreed qualifications, confirmed against the index.

checklist.step: Execute the certifications by February 1
actions: Review each draft against the support-file index and the deficiency memorandum before signing — the signature asserts personal knowledge of program compliance.
Execute via DocuSign (or wet ink where a state requires it) with the correct officer title per state.
Where a state requires a different officer (e.g. a designated executive), route to that signer with the same review pack.
Return executed originals to the Compliance Manager by February 1.
checklist.done: every required certification is executed by the correct officer by February 1 after review against the support file.

checklist.step: Submit to each domiciliary commissioner by the deadline
actions: File each executed certification through the state's recorded channel — DOI electronic filing portal, designated email, or certified mail to the commissioner's office — no later than February 10, holding the final days as buffer against the February 15 statutory date.
Capture proof per submission: portal confirmation number, delivery receipt or certified-mail tracking showing receipt on or before the due date.
Log each proof into the tracker row and mark the pair complete.
Same-day escalate to the CISO and Regulatory Counsel any channel failure (portal outage, bounced address) so an alternate route lands inside the deadline.
checklist.done: every entity/state pair shows a logged filing proof dated on or before its due date.

checklist.step: Handle non-standard and newly adopting states
actions: For any state whose adoption sets a variant due date, filer class or content, verify the tracker row carried the variant and the filing matched it.
For states adopting Model 668 mid-year, compute the first-certification due date from the enacted transition provisions and add the row to next cycle's calendar.
Update the variance appendix with any certification-requirement change discovered during the cycle.
Brief the Compliance Manager so no first-time certification is discovered in February.
checklist.done: variant and first-time certification requirements are captured in the tracker before their first due date.

checklist.step: Confirm and file the 5-year support record
actions: File each executed certification with its filing proof and the indexed support file under REG-052-C05/<year>/<entity>.
Apply the 5-year retention label per Section 4(i) so the record survives for commissioner examination.
Verify retrieval by entity, state and year in one search.
Restrict write access so the support file is immutable after filing.
checklist.done: certifications, proofs and support files are retained 5 years, immutable and retrievable by entity, state and year.

checklist.step: Arm next year's reminders immediately
actions: Roll the tracker rows forward to next year's due dates the week after submission closes.
Re-arm the T-90 through T-3 reminder chain against February 15 (and each variant date).
Diarise the November 15 cycle-open task to the Compliance Manager.
Record the roll-forward so the calendar handoff is examinable.
checklist.done: next cycle's rows, reminders and open task are armed within a week of submission close.

checklist.step: Log any late, missed or qualified filing as an exception
actions: Raise a tracker exception for any submission after the due date, any missed entity/state pair, and any certification qualified for a material gap.
For late or missed filings, have Regulatory Counsel assess the curative path — immediate filing with an explanatory cover to the commissioner — and execute it within 5 business days.
Assign root cause (calendar miss, channel failure, evidence hole, signing delay) and an owner.
Report the exception summary to the CISO and the security governance committee.
checklist.done: every miss carries an exception with root cause, a counsel-directed cure executed within 5 business days, and committee visibility.

checklist.step: Reconcile the certification against the incident-year record
actions: Before the cycle closes, re-read each executed statement against the year's cybersecurity-event register (REG-052-C04) and the exception registers to confirm nothing filed contradicts the record.
Where a post-signing fact emerges that makes a statement inaccurate, advise on the correction filing to the commissioner rather than leaving the record wrong.
Document the reconciliation conclusion in a memo to the support file.
Flag any pattern (repeated qualifications, recurring gaps) to the CISO for the next program cycle.
checklist.done: a counsel memo confirms each filed statement reconciles to the year's record or a correction was filed.

checklist.step: Track amendments to certification requirements through the year
actions: Monitor state DOI bulletins and legislative feeds for changes to certification forms, due dates or filer classes among the 44 adopting jurisdictions.
Log each confirmed change into the variance appendix and the tracker rows within 10 business days.
Notify the Compliance Manager of any change landing inside an open cycle.
Re-verify the full requirement set annually at cycle open.
checklist.done: requirement changes reach the appendix and tracker within 10 business days and the set is re-verified each cycle.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with CISO sign-off
actions: Review the completed tracker (all pairs filed, proofs logged), the exception register and the counsel reconciliation memo.
Sign the cycle-closure memo stating every required certification was filed on time and supported, or naming the cures executed.
File the signed memo in the support file and brief the board risk committee in the next Section 4(e) report.
Hand carry-over improvement items into the WISP annual review.
checklist.done: a signed closure memo confirms complete, supported filings (or executed cures) and feeds the board report.

testing.step: Build the entity/state population independently
actions: Obtain the insurer legal-entity register directly from the Corporate Secretary (not from the compliance tracker) with each entity's domicile and NAIC co-code.
Independently determine each domiciliary state's certification requirement and due date from current statute text, not from the variance appendix.
Construct the auditor's own required-filing list as the test population.
testing.done: an independently constructed entity/state required-filing list exists with statutory due dates.

testing.step: Reconcile the auditor's list to the compliance tracker
actions: Compare the auditor's required-filing list to the tracker rows the cycle actually worked.
Investigate every difference: a pair the tracker missed is an automatic exception; a pair the tracker worked that the auditor's list omits gets the statute re-read before dismissal.
Confirm 'not required' conclusions in the tracker carry a citation.
testing.done: the tracker and the independent list agree or every difference is dispositioned with citations.

testing.step: Trace every filing to dated proof
actions: For 100% of required pairs (the population is small enough that sampling is unjustified), open the filing proof — portal confirmation, delivery receipt or certified-mail tracking — and read the received date.
Compare each received date to the state's statutory due date; compute days early or late.
Verify the proof names the correct entity, NAIC co-code and certification period.
Any proof dated after the due date, or any pair with no proof, is an automatic exception.
testing.done: every required pair traces to a proof dated on or before its statutory due date with correct entity data.

testing.step: Re-perform the requirement lookup for a state sample
actions: For the domiciliary states filed plus 3 'not required' conclusions, read the state's enacted Section 4(i) analogue at source and independently conclude on requirement, due date, filer and channel.
Compare to what the cycle executed; a filing made to the wrong office or on the wrong form is an exception even if timely.
Capture the statute text relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled states show independently verified requirement, date, filer and channel matching what was executed.

testing.step: Walk the support file behind each statement
actions: For each executed certification, walk the support-file index clause by clause and open the evidence behind each certified assertion (WISP approval, risk assessment, control metrics, event register).
Confirm each cited artifact is in-period and final, not draft.
A certified clause resting on missing, stale or draft evidence is an exception against the statement's accuracy.
testing.done: every certified clause traces to final, in-period evidence through the index.

testing.step: Test the deficiency documentation behind any known gaps
actions: Compare the year's exception registers and audit findings (C01-C04) to the deficiency-and-remediation memorandum in the support file.
Confirm every material gap open at signing appears in the memorandum with documented remediation efforts, per Section 4(i)'s record requirement.
A material gap absent from the memorandum — meaning the officer certified without the remediation record — is a critical exception.
Verify counsel's agreed statement effect (qualification or none) was actually reflected in the filed text.
testing.done: every material gap open at signing is covered by the remediation record and the filed text reflects the agreed treatment.

testing.step: Recompute the milestone and deadline maths
actions: Recompute the cycle milestones (cycle open T-92, evidence January 15, execution February 1, submission February 10) against the actual completion dates in the tracker.
Verify the reminder chain fired by inspecting the tracker notification log.
Note milestone slippage that compressed the counsel-review or signing window as a process finding even where the filing landed on time.
testing.done: milestone actuals and reminder firings are recomputed, with compression noted as findings.

testing.step: Verify signer authority and execution integrity
actions: Open the DocuSign envelope audit trail for each executed certification and verify the signer identity, title and signing timestamp.
Confirm the signer matches the state's required officer class and that signing followed the CISO's documented review of the support-file index.
An execution by an unauthorized title, or a signing timestamp preceding the support file's completion, is an exception.
testing.done: each execution shows an authorized signer, post-review timing and an intact envelope audit trail.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the entity, state, what failed and the regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (population miss, late proof, unsupported clause, missing deficiency record, wrong signer) and an owner with a date.
For any missed or inaccurate filing, confirm the counsel-directed cure (late filing with cover, or correction filing) was executed and logged.
Carry open items into next March's verification as mandatory retests.
testing.done: each exception is tracked with root cause and owner, and filing failures show executed cures.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the certification verification
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (any missing/late proof, unsupported clause or undocumented material gap fails).
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with per-entity workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer having assembled no support file and drafted no statement, and file under REG-052-C05/<year>/test.
Report to the audit committee and the CISO in March, while curative filings remain credible.
testing.done: a signed March workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to committee and CISO.

checklist.step: Build and maintain the nonpublic-information vendor register
actions: Extract the active vendor master from Coupa/Ariba and screen every vendor for whether it maintains, processes, stores or can access nonpublic information — data processors, claims TPAs, print/mail houses, cloud hosts, IT support with production access, offsite storage.
Cross-check against accounts-payable spend and the CMDB integration list so vendors paid outside procurement or connected without contracts still surface.
Load the confirmed population into the GRC TPSP register with service description, data classes touched and business owner.
Refresh the screen quarterly and on every new-vendor request.
checklist.done: a quarterly-refreshed register lists every vendor touching nonpublic information, reconciled to spend and integrations.

checklist.step: Risk-tier every registered vendor
actions: Apply the four-tier model in the GRC platform: Tier 1 (bulk consumer nonpublic information or production system access), Tier 2 (limited nonpublic information), Tier 3 (incidental access), Tier 4 (none — monitored for scope creep).
Record the tiering rationale on each vendor row so the call is reproducible.
Re-tier on any service change, and treat a vendor's scope creep from Tier 3 into data access as a new onboarding event.
Publish the tier counts to the CISO quarterly.
checklist.done: every registered vendor carries a tier with recorded rationale, re-tiered on service change.

checklist.step: Run due diligence before selection and before access
actions: For each new Tier 1/2 vendor, issue the security questionnaire through the GRC platform covering the Section 4(d) safeguard set — access control, encryption, MFA, monitoring, disposal — as applied to the licensee's data.
For Tier 1, obtain and review the current SOC 2 Type II report: read the auditor's opinion, test exceptions and the complementary user-entity controls (CUECs), and map each CUEC to an internal owner.
Score the assessment, document residual concerns and record the approve/conditional/reject decision with the approver's name.
Gate the procurement workflow so no contract signature or system access precedes an approved assessment — wire the Coupa approval chain to require the GRC assessment id.
checklist.done: no new vendor gains signature or access without a scored, approved assessment, with Tier 1 SOC 2 reviews and CUEC ownership mapped.

checklist.step: Embed the Section 4(f) safeguard clause set in every contract
actions: Maintain the standard clause set in the Icertis clause library: the vendor must implement appropriate administrative, technical and physical measures to protect the licensee's information systems and nonpublic information, aligned to Model 668 Section 4(f).
Include audit/assessment rights, subcontractor flow-down of the same obligations, data-return-or-destruction on termination and breach-cost allocation.
Tag every nonpublic-information vendor contract in the CLM with the clause-compliance status so gaps are queryable.
Require Legal sign-off on any negotiated deviation from the standard clauses, recorded against the contract.
checklist.done: every nonpublic-information vendor contract carries the tagged safeguard clause set or a Legal-approved recorded deviation.

checklist.step: Require vendor breach notification fast enough to protect the 72-hour duty
actions: Include in every nonpublic-information vendor contract a clause obliging the vendor to notify the licensee's security contact of any cybersecurity event without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 48 hours after discovery — leaving headroom inside the licensee's own 72-hour commissioner clock under Section 6(d).
Specify the notice channel (the security intake mailbox and the 24x7 SOC line) and the minimum facts required (systems, data classes, period, consumer counts).
Verify the clause survives vendor paper — a vendor's own template usually says 'commercially reasonable time' and must be struck.
Tag notice-clause status in the CLM alongside the safeguard tag.
checklist.done: every contract carries a 48-hour vendor-notice clause with a named channel, tagged and queryable in the CLM.

checklist.step: Remediate the legacy contract book
actions: Query the CLM for active nonpublic-information vendor contracts missing either tag and rank them by tier and renewal date.
Amend Tier 1 gaps proactively via addendum rather than waiting for renewal; fold Tier 2/3 fixes into the renewal cycle with the 90-day CLM flag.
Track the remediation burn-down monthly to the Third-Party Risk Manager.
Register any vendor refusing the clauses as a GRC exception for a risk-based retain/replace decision by the CISO.
checklist.done: the clause-gap book burns down on schedule, with Tier 1 gaps amended proactively and refusals escalated to the CISO.

checklist.step: Run periodic reassessments on cadence
actions: Work the GRC reassessment queue: Tier 1 annually and Tier 2 biennially from each vendor's anniversary, launched at the T-60 reminder.
For Tier 1, collect the fresh SOC 2 Type II (or bridge letter covering the gap period), re-run the questionnaire delta and re-verify CUEC ownership.
Close each reassessment with an updated score and decision; chase overdue vendors weekly and escalate any assessment 30 days past anniversary to the Third-Party Risk Manager.
File reassessment evidence in the compliance evidence repository per vendor.
checklist.done: Tier 1 and Tier 2 reassessments complete on cadence with fresh SOC 2 coverage and filed evidence, overdues escalated.

checklist.step: Track vendor findings to remediation
actions: Register every material finding from assessments and SOC 2 exceptions as a GRC item with the vendor's committed remediation date.
Chase vendor evidence of closure and verify it rather than accepting attestation alone for Tier 1 findings.
Apply compensating controls on the licensee side (restricted data feeds, enhanced monitoring) while findings stay open.
Escalate any Tier 1 finding open past 90 days to the CISO with a retain/restrict/exit recommendation.
checklist.done: every vendor finding is tracked to verified closure or an escalated retain/restrict/exit decision.

checklist.step: Operate the vendor-event intake into the incident process
actions: Monitor the security intake mailbox and SOC line for vendor breach notices and open a ServiceNow security-incident ticket the same day, tagged to the vendor register row.
Hand the ticket to the Incident Response Lead so the licensee's own determination and 72-hour analysis run under REG-052-C04 on the licensee's clock.
Demand the contractual minimum facts from the vendor and log each follow-up; a vendor slow-rolling facts does not pause the licensee's obligations.
Record the event against the vendor for the next reassessment and the retain/exit file.
checklist.done: vendor notices become same-day incident tickets feeding the REG-052-C04 determination, with facts chased and the vendor record updated.

checklist.step: Watch for vendor incidents the vendor did not report
actions: Screen threat-intelligence and news feeds weekly for breaches at registered vendors and their material subcontractors.
On a hit, open an inquiry to the vendor citing the contract's notice clause and ask for written confirmation of impact on the licensee's data within 5 business days.
Escalate non-responsive vendors to the Third-Party Risk Manager and treat credible unconfirmed exposure as an incident-process trigger.
Log every screen and inquiry so the monitoring is evidenced, not anecdotal.
checklist.done: weekly screens are logged and every external hit produced a time-bound vendor inquiry with escalation on silence.

checklist.step: Enforce subcontractor flow-down
actions: Require Tier 1 vendors to disclose subcontractors that touch the licensee's nonpublic information, at onboarding and at each reassessment.
Verify the contract's flow-down clause obliges equivalent safeguards and notice duties on those subcontractors.
Record material subcontractors on the vendor's register row so fourth-party concentration is visible.
Challenge any new undisclosed subcontractor discovered via SOC 2 or incident facts as a contract breach.
checklist.done: Tier 1 subcontractors are disclosed, flow-down verified and recorded, with undisclosed discoveries treated as breaches.

checklist.step: Offboard with data return or destruction
actions: On contract termination, trigger the offboarding checklist: revoke system access and integration credentials the same day via the IAM team, and invoke the data-return-or-destruction clause.
Collect the vendor's destruction certificate (media, method, date, signatory) or return manifest within 30 days of termination.
Verify no residual feeds or accounts survive by checking the integration list and Okta application assignments.
File the certificate in the compliance evidence repository against the vendor and close the register row.
checklist.done: terminated vendors show same-day access revocation and a filed destruction certificate or return manifest within 30 days.

checklist.step: Report the TPSP risk posture quarterly
actions: Publish the quarterly dashboard: register size by tier, assessment currency, clause-gap burn-down, open findings by age, vendor events and offboarding compliance.
Present it to the CISO and the security governance committee with the top vendor risks narrated.
Feed the material third-party arrangements summary into the annual Section 4(e) board report and the certification support file.
Archive each quarter's pack in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: a quarterly posture pack reaches the CISO and committee and feeds the board report and certification file.

checklist.step: Log program exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a GRC exception for any vendor onboarded before assessment, contract missing clauses beyond plan, reassessment 30+ days overdue, or missing destruction certificate.
Assign root cause, owner, compensating control and remediation date.
Review open exceptions monthly and escalate Tier 1 items to the CISO.
Surface the exception register in the certification support file.
checklist.done: every program deviation is a tracked exception with compensating control and certification-file visibility.

checklist.step: Close the year with CISO sign-off
actions: Review the year-end register health, exception ledger and vendor-event record with the Third-Party Risk Manager.
Sign remediation closures on Tier 1 exceptions and set dates on carry-overs.
Confirm the TPSP posture supports the February 15 certification or direct its inclusion in the deficiency memorandum.
File the signed year-end review in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed year-end review closes or carries over Tier 1 exceptions and states certification impact.

testing.step: Build the vendor population from independent sources
actions: Extract the active vendor master from Coupa/Ariba, the trailing-12-month accounts-payable spend file and the CMDB third-party integration list.
Union the three sources into an independent candidate list of vendors plausibly touching nonpublic information.
Baseline counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent three-source vendor candidate list is built and baselined.

testing.step: Reconcile the candidate list to the TPSP register
actions: Match every candidate vendor to a register row or a documented out-of-scope conclusion.
Investigate unmatched candidates with the business owner — a claims TPA or print house paid through AP but absent from the register is an automatic exception.
Check register rows with no matching spend or integration for staleness.
testing.done: every candidate maps to a register row or a documented conclusion, with unregistered data-touching vendors as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the vendor sample
actions: Take 100% of Tier 1 vendors, 15 random Tier 2/3 vendors (seeded, reproducible), all vendors onboarded in the year and all vendors offboarded in the year.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date.
Exclude no vendor for sensitivity — strategic vendors are where oversight most often softens.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all Tier 1, a random lower-tier cut and the full onboarding/offboarding cohorts.

testing.step: Re-perform the tiering judgement
actions: For 15 sampled vendors, read the service description and data classes, then independently assign a tier before looking at the recorded one.
Compare; an under-tiered vendor (assessed lighter than its data access warrants) is an exception with cascade effect on assessment cadence.
Check re-tiering happened on sampled vendors whose services changed in-year.
testing.done: sampled tier calls are independently reproduced or logged as exceptions with cascade noted.

testing.step: Trace contracts to the safeguard and notice clauses
actions: For each sampled vendor, open the executed contract in the CLM and locate the Section 4(f) safeguard clause, the 48-hour breach-notice clause, the flow-down and the destruction-on-exit clause in the actual signed text — not the tag.
Compare the signed text to the CLM tag; a tag claiming compliance over absent or diluted text is a double exception (clause gap plus data-integrity failure).
Verify recorded deviations carry Legal sign-off.
Capture the clause pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled contracts show the four clauses in signed text matching their tags, with deviations Legal-approved.

testing.step: Verify due-diligence timing on the onboarding cohort
actions: For every vendor onboarded in the year, compare the assessment approval date to the contract signature date and to the first system-access or data-feed date from IAM and integration logs.
Any access or signature preceding an approved assessment is an automatic exception — the gate either held or it did not.
For Tier 1 onboards, verify the SOC 2 Type II review memo exists with CUEC ownership mapped.
testing.done: every onboarded vendor shows assessment approval preceding both signature and access, with Tier 1 SOC 2 memos on file.

testing.step: Test reassessment currency and finding remediation
actions: For each Tier 1 vendor, compute months since the last completed reassessment and flag anything over 12; for sampled Tier 2, over 24.
For 10 sampled findings, verify closure evidence is vendor-supplied artifact (config proof, retest) not bare attestation, and that compensating controls operated while open.
A Tier 1 finding open past 90 days without a CISO-level retain/restrict/exit decision is an exception.
testing.done: reassessment currency recomputes within cadence and sampled findings show verified closures or escalated decisions.

testing.step: Trace vendor events and offboarding execution
actions: For every vendor breach notice received in the year, trace intake to a same-day ServiceNow ticket and onward into the REG-052-C04 determination record.
For every offboarded vendor, verify same-day access revocation in the IAM logs and a destruction certificate or return manifest filed within 30 days.
Cross-check the weekly external-monitoring log for screened vendor breaches and confirm each hit produced a time-bound inquiry.
A vendor event that never reached the incident process is a critical exception.
testing.done: vendor events trace into the incident process and offboardings show revocation plus 30-day certificates.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception naming the vendor, the failure and the nonpublic-information exposure.
Assign root cause (register gap, gate bypass, clause dilution, cadence slip, offboarding miss) and an owner with a date.
Route any exception indicating actual data exposure to the Incident Response Lead for determination under REG-052-C04.
Carry open items into the quarterly onboarding spot-checks as mandatory retests.
testing.done: each exception carries root cause, owner and date, with exposure-bearing items routed to incident determination.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the TPSP verification
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (any stale Tier 1 assessment, missing clause, gate bypass or missing destruction certificate fails).
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with per-vendor workpaper references.
Sign as independent reviewer having assessed no sampled vendor and negotiated no sampled contract, and file under REG-052-C06/<year>/test.
Report to the audit committee and the CISO ahead of the February 15 certification.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported before certification.
